records.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse

scope_advice.object: memory content, current context, KV cache ranges and selected pre-existing LoRA adapter
scope_advice.feedback: fixed schema compatibility and reconciliation rules react to context changes; no evidence they rewrite the memory management algorithm or prompt policy based on success
scope_advice.retention: KV state and memory content reuse, not acceptance of new Harness artifacts
scope_advice.why_zh: HeMeR 是固定缓存协调算法；上下文变化与 adapter 切换触发既定操作，未展示反馈改写管理机制或指令。不能把记忆内容更新、缓存状态复用等同 Harness 演化。
limits: 不否认存在动态记忆和 LoRA procedures；排除的是本文自我修改 Harness 机制的证据不足。
本文主要评估推理成本与任务成功，不是自改管理机制的专项评测。

evidence.quote: We distinguish three levels of memory representation: memory modules, memory contents, and memory contexts. A memory module stores and retrieves a specific type of information, and each item retrieved at a decision step is a memory content. A memory context is formed by composing multiple memory contents to support action selection. In our setting, the agent uses declarative, procedural, and working memory modules. Declarative memory stores explicit task and environment knowledge, such as object locations, receptacle relations, and task conditions. Procedural memory stores reusable behavioral procedures, instantiated as LoRA adapters in our LRAgent-based implementation [ 14 ] . Working memory stores the current interaction state, including recent observations, intermediate decisions, subgoals, and action history.

To address this trade-off, HeMeR uses the chunk-level index to compare memory chunks across consecutive decision steps. Chunks in X_{t-1} and X_{t} are first matched by persistent chunk IDs, regardless of their positions or token spans. Matched chunks are eligible for KV reuse only when their memory module type, semantic role, dependency annotation, normalized content, and adapter identifier (when applicable) agree. Otherwise, their KV ranges are locally recomputed. Given two consecutive memory contexts, HeMeR computes a schema-guided reconciliation plan \Delta_{t}=\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathcal{S}}(X_{t-1},X_{t}), (6) where \mathrm{Diff}_{\mathcal{S}} matches chunks by persistent IDs and checks schema compatibility. Matched chunks with changed positions are reordered, chunks only in X_{t} are inserted, and chunks only in X_{t-1} are evicted. The index maps these operations to KV ranges, so HeMeR updates only affected ranges.

Algorithm 1 summarizes the inference procedure of HeMeR . At each decision step, the agent first obtains memory contents from declarative, procedural, and working memory modules and forms the memory context X_{t} . Instead of rebuilding the full KV cache for X_{t} , HeMeR compares the current memory context with the previous one using schema fields attached to each memory chunk. The resulting reconciliation plan identifies inserted, evicted, and reordered chunks, maps these operations to KV ranges, and determines which cached states can be reused. A cached KV range is reused only when the corresponding memory content remains compatible under the schema. If the chunk is unchanged but only its position changes, HeMeR applies RoPE-based remapping to correct the positional phase of cached key states. If the memory content, dependency annotation, or adapter identifier changes, the affected KV range is locally recomputed to avoid stale reuse.

We document the prompt templates used in our experiments. The system prompt, task brief, action grammar, and observation-action format are shared across methods within each benchmark. Methods differ only in whether and how they use the provided memory contents, and in how their serving policy reuses or recomputes KV states. This ensures that performance differences are not caused by benchmark-specific prompt engineering. Although the prompt template is shown in full, cache-reuse methods do not prefill the entire rendered prompt at every decision step. TTFT includes KV cache updates, required prefill, and local recomputation up to the first generated token, excluding memory retrieval, prompt construction, and schema-diff planning.

scope_advice.object: output game-player networks/weights or Python programs, not the writer agent Harness
scope_advice.feedback: up to three support-level feedback resubmissions revise the game-solving artifact
scope_advice.retention: final generated player reused on held-out episodes within game families; not retained edits to writer prompt/tool workflow
scope_advice.why_zh: 确有反馈修订与留出评测，但修改对象是任务要求生成的游戏程序/网络；不据此标 writer 自身 Harness 演化。
limits: 写网络权重属于输出产物；不能自动算模型递归自训练，更不能算 Harness coevolution。
FreeArch 为探索性条件，学习者与 writer 获得信息不同；不扩展到一般模型训练结论。

evidence.quote: Written weights , one-shot ( W1 ) or with feedback ( W2 ): the writer returns build() , which constructs all tensors of the fixed actor. A sandbox prohibits training, fitting, searching over weights and simulating the game (Appendix A.5 ). Feedback allows up to three resubmissions, each after an outcome table on the support starts and up to three failure reports (frames, action traces and, for networks, logits and channel maxima).

The four main writers are GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra and Claude Opus 5.5. The five weaker writers are GPT-6 Luna, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5 and the previous-generation GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5. All run at reasoning effort high , without tools, with the same prompt: the mechanics-only source and the engine base class, the support start observations, the episode rules and, for the weights conditions, the actor’s exact NumPy reference (Appendices A.3 and A.4 ).

These results suggest a hypothesis about how weight-space programming works: the writer first derives a symbolic solution and then expresses it in weights, so that what it writes is a program even when the output is a network. Earlier demonstrations fit this reading. Takehi et al. (2026) describe their writer as converting “desired programs” into neural form for public games with known rules, and where no algorithm is known, written models are built from hand-designed interpretable features ( Singh et al., 2026 ) . Their written transformers for language tasks have the same signature as our networks: rebuilding 21 of their 24 released language-task models from their code, we find 99% of the parameters exactly zero and 95% of the rest small integers or powers of two (Appendix B ). Our evidence comes from games whose perception, although it must be computed at run time, can be specified exactly from the rendering code, and whose policies admit a compact program. Tasks whose perception is statistical rather than exact, such as natural images, would test the hypothesis, and tasks with dense rewards, where RL fine-tuning works well, would test whether writing and training can combine.

records.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents

scope_advice.object: governance of persistent changes to prompts/policies/tools/orchestration, among a general agent configuration
scope_advice.feedback: fresh paired confirmatory audit plus candidate-specific independent evaluator calibration; reference-relative non-inferiority and mandatory checks
scope_advice.retention: proposed immutable candidate committed only after statistical/governance and bounded canary gates; formal protocol, not executed agent evidence
scope_advice.why_zh: 理论直接针对自生成外部配置修改的持久准入、跨候选选择偏差和参考漂移，可纳入 Harness 专项理论。真实 Agent 上的改进/安全尚未验证，不按演化方法实证计数。
limits: Monte Carlo 是合成统计实验，不是部署 Agent 实验。
保证以独立新审查/校准样本、同分布、有限预定指标与参考程序有效性为条件；不等于通用安全。
不代表已证明真实部署中长期单调提升；校准分布错配时作者模拟全部campaign错误接受。
只核范围、定理陈述的条件与文章可见结果；未形式化校验全部证明或重跑模拟。

evidence.quote: Given experience \mathcal{E}_{j} , a candidate generator produces \widetilde{A}_{j}=\mathcal{U}(I_{j},\mathcal{E}_{j}). (2) The generator may be an optimiser, an LLM-based editor, a search procedure, or a human-supervised process. EGE does not prescribe the generator.

A candidate is evidence-governed if it is frozen before its audit sample is drawn, evaluated using fresh audit observations not used to construct or tune that candidate, and assessed using prespecified metrics, margins, and governance checks.

The theorem controls simultaneous statistical undercoverage relative to the reference-evaluation estimand. It does not prove that the reference evaluator measures the intended real-world capability, that the audit distribution matches deployment, or that an agent cannot cause harm through unmeasured actions. Those are separate validity and governance questions.

The operational state machine has four states: (1) Candidate , where a proposed modification is frozen; (2) Audit-passed , where statistical and governance requirements pass; (3) Canary , where the candidate runs under bounded traffic, permissions, workload, or execution scope; and (4) Committed , where it becomes the persistent configuration after prespecified canary criteria pass.

We ran a targeted Monte Carlo sensitivity study to examine two distinct properties of the proposed gate: (i) whether candidate-specific calibration prevents harmful acceptance when the operational evaluator is optimistic, and (ii) how much acceptance power is lost when calibration and audit samples are small. This is a synthetic statistical experiment, not an autonomous-agent benchmark. Each condition comprises 3,000 independent campaigns with 10 candidates per campaign. Each candidate is beneficial or harmful with probability one half. The reference-procedure primary effect is +0.25 for beneficial candidates and -0.10 for harmful candidates; the protected effect is zero. The primary threshold is \delta=0.05 , the protected non-inferiority margin is \epsilon=0.20 , and the global error budget is \alpha=0.05 . The operational evaluator’s primary-score optimism is varied over b\in\{0,0.10,0.25\} ; protected-metric bias is zero. Confirmatory paired differences are sampled from \{-1,+1\} with the specified means, while calibration discrepancies are sampled from \{-2,+2\} with the specified mean. The confirmatory and calibration samples are independent. We vary both sample sizes together over n=m\in\{5{,}000,20{,}000,80{,}000\} per candidate and metric. The candidate-wise evaluation and calibration allocations are each 3\alpha/(\pi^{2}j^{2}R) , so the two families jointly consume the global error budget. The random seed is 20261112.

The guarantee assumes bounded paired observations and conditionally independent fresh confirmatory and calibration samples. Real agent tasks may be dependent, nonstationary, or affected by shared infrastructure. The reference-evaluation procedure must be sufficiently valid for the intended construct; the theorem only controls discrepancy relative to that procedure. Candidate-specific calibration is sample-intensive, and the Monte Carlo study is a stylised stress test rather than a real-agent evaluation. Extensions to clustered sampling, martingale differences, nonstationary evaluation, and efficient uniform calibration over candidate classes are important. A reference can become obsolete; the bridge-test result controls only declared metrics on a common distribution. Configuration rollback cannot undo external actions. The immediate empirical priority is to implement the protocol in a representative agent system and measure both audit cost and operational outcomes.

records.title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents

scope_advice.object: controller(obs) Python file controlling a physical/simulated plant
scope_advice.feedback: visible-seed grader and local simulations revise controller task artifact; separate held-out grader
scope_advice.retention: some lower-tier controller files transferred to harder tiers, while coding agent Harness stays unchanged
scope_advice.why_zh: agent 的外层 Harness 固定；被写入、调参和跨任务传递的是被要求设计的物理控制器。不能把 control policy 任务产物误当 LLM agent 的控制流。
limits: 保留有执行反馈和 controller handoff 的事实，排除不依赖是否存在反馈。
与 Harness 自我修改专项评测不同；三次会话是计数，不是稳健总体成功率。

evidence.quote: Three models were run as coding agents under one protocol: Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1, 5 5 5 Claude Fable 5.2 was released on 9 November 2026, after the sessions reported here were run. each through the Claude Code harness at its highest reasoning effort, without network access, launched by Harbor. A session is one container, one instruction, one hour from the agent’s first command and one graded file. The instruction states the budget, a score of zero for any submission below the gate, and the command to read the clock. Three sessions were run per task and model, so 2/3 means two of them passed. Opus and Fable ran on all 44 tasks and Sonnet on the 22 MuJoCo tasks, 330 sessions in all, each sandbox limited to two cores and 2 GB.

Here the agent is a language model operating a terminal, its actions are shell commands and file edits, an episode is a session with a wall-clock budget, and the reward is computed once, at the end, on seeds the agent never sees. Nothing is learned inside this loop: the session trains no neural network and runs no reinforcement-learning algorithm. It leaves a controller file behind. The RL solution of Section 4 and the coding agent thus act at different levels, one learning the controller from millions of plant steps, the other writing it as code after a few hundred plant episodes, and both are graded by the same inner-loop gate on the same seeds. A Harbor task carries a verifiable scalar reward, thus the tasks can also be used as reinforcement learning environments for post-training of language models.

The artefact is one Python file exporting one function, controller(obs) , from the plant’s output to an action array, and the starting file applies zero action. The instruction states the plant, its observation and action, the ladder of requirements and the grader’s flags, and imposes two rules: no neural networks and no gradient-based learning, so that the artefact stays a program an engineer can read, and a budget of one hour from the agent’s first command, with a submission below the gate scoring zero. The sandbox is a container with the plant package installed and no network; the hidden reference controllers are stripped from the image. The agent has the evaluator itself as a tool, on visible seeds disjoint from the held-out ones, and a parameter tuner that searches a declared PARAMS block with a declared budget. It has no clock other than the shell and is told to run date , which gives it a precise reading of the time. Grading runs in a separate container on the submitted file alone, with a budget of 15 minutes.

We set out to test what current frontier coding agents can do when asked to design a controller. For that test we propose a Harbor task format: 44 tasks over 13 plants, so that any agent harness runs against them unchanged. A task grades one file as control engineers grade, on held-out seeds, against a ladder of named requirements, under perturbation suites and certificates, within an hour. Under one protocol, three frontier models designed controllers that reach the return of an RL solution on every plant where the gate asks for it, even though in a minority of sessions; the controllers are programs of tens to hundreds of lines that an engineer can read. On the four plants that carry an RL solution, one evaluation of the reference controller is 2 to 40 times faster than one evaluation of the RL network, measured on CPU. Robustness appeared only when the specification demanded it, and it was then within reach of a textbook design, on the humanoid at the RL solution’s own return, where a domain-randomised RL solution falls short; designs whose gains came from in-session search were as brittle as the RL solutions they match. Two tasks remain open for the designed route: the humanoid under 100 N pushes, and the same plant under those pushes together with torso mass +20\,\% , friction -30\,\% , motors -20\,\% , gravity +10\,\% , measurement noise and one-step command delay. The second remains open for the RL route as well.

records.title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution

scope_advice.object: textual skill-library and compositions plus an execution protocol skill compiled from observed failure types; fixed backbone
scope_advice.feedback: training rollout F1, contrastive step alignment and model-judged candidate probes; failure types add protocol instructions; rewards update/prune library
scope_advice.retention: library rewritten batch by batch and frozen for reuse on held-out test questions; protocol skill injected into future questions/tool turns
scope_advice.why_zh: 原文不仅给经验打分：按训练失败类型构造后续执行所用 protocol instruction，并迭代接纳/组织可重用策略技能，固定模型权重，满足组件 Harness 演化。应说明技能主体是文本策略，C3执行选项是固定配置；不把 hypergraph 的权重叫模型权重。
limits: 技能以name/description文本策略为主；counterfactual probe是同一模型对假设的YES/NO判断，不是对所有候选进行真实执行干预。
每格一次评测；总体领先混合 C1/C2 与额外 C3格式修复、搜索、token/投票预算差异，不能称同预算技能改进因果效果。
只看到图表文字与方法/附录文本，未重算全部收益、开销或图像数据。
技能、边权、排序优势不是基础模型权重更新；不可归 weight-Harness coevolution。

evidence.quote: Problem Formulation. Unlike the methods of Table 1 , HyperSkill couples a per-skill quality signal with explicit multi-skill compositions in a weighted skill hypergraph. Formally, let \pi_{\theta} be a frozen omnimodal backbone whose parameters \theta are never updated, and let \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{train}} and \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}} be train and test sets of triples (q,a^{*},m) , in which each query q carries a gold answer a^{*} and a modality tag m\!\in\!\mathcal{M}\!=\!\{\text{text},\text{image},\text{pdf},\text{video},\text{audio}\} . We seek a weighted skill hypergraph \mathcal{H}\!=\!(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E},w) in which every node v_{i}\!\in\!\mathcal{V} carries a name, a description and an advantage u_{i}\!\in\![-1,1] , and every hyperedge e_{j}\!\in\!\mathcal{E} groups |e_{j}|\!\geq\!2 nodes into a joint composition with weight w(e_{j}) . We also seek a retriever \mathcal{R}\!:\!(q,m,\mathcal{H})\!\to\!\mathcal{S}_{q}\!\subset\!\mathcal{V} under which the skill-augmented policy improves on its skill-free version, while a hypergraph update \mathcal{U} replaces the gradient step in every round t : \bigl(\mathcal{H}^{\star},\,\mathcal{R}^{\star}\bigr)\;=\;\arg\!\max_{\mathcal{H},\,\mathcal{R}}\;\mathbb{E}_{(q,a^{*},m)\sim\mathcal{D}}\!\Bigl[\,r\bigl(\,\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\!\mid\!q,m,\mathcal{R}(q,m,\mathcal{H}))\,;\,a^{*}\,\bigr)\,\Bigr]\,,\quad\mathcal{H}_{t+1}\!=\!\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{H}_{t};\mathcal{B}_{t})\,, (1) where \mathcal{D} is the task distribution ( \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{train}} in training, \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}} at evaluation), \mathcal{B}_{t} the round- t training batch and r the token-level F_{1} reward against a^{*} . Unlike GRPO, the optimisation variable is the pair (\mathcal{H},\mathcal{R}) rather than \theta : gradient updates are replaced by an iterative, auditable rewrite of the library. C1 (§ 3.1 ) handles gaps (i) and (ii), C2 (§ 3.2 ) handles gap (iii), and C3 (§ 3.3 ) fixes execution failures of the frozen backbone; Figure 3 gives an overview of how C1 and C2 build, evolve and query the library.

Protocol Skill and Answer Form. A frozen backbone often breaks the tool or answer format, not the task. C1 therefore sorts every training rollout that ends without an answer into four failure types: malformed tool call, call beyond the budget, call without tools, and no <answer> tag. Each tool-related type seen in at least 2 rollouts adds fixed instruction lines, filled with the dataset’s tool tags and budget, to a protocol skill . Its last line fixes the answer form: the integer without \boxed{} on math, else a short answer or, per dataset, a form derived from the training gold answers (option letter, phrase or sentence, plus an abstention line). The protocol skill is not a node of \mathcal{H} (App. A ).

Counterfactual Verification. Step alignment alone still admits skills that merely correlate with success; we therefore pair each candidate with a list \mathcal{P}_{q} of at most K failure probes o^{-}\!\in\!\mathcal{O}_{q}^{-} of its own question and ask the same frozen \pi_{\theta} a binary counterfactual probe [ 42 , 28 , 40 ] : “had the agent known \widetilde{v} , would o^{-} likely have produced a^{*} ?”. Only when a strict majority of the probes return YES is the candidate admitted into the round- t skill increment, and a deterministic identifier \mathrm{sid}(\widetilde{v})\!=\!\mathrm{md5}(\mathrm{name}(\widetilde{v})) deduplicates it against the current library \mathcal{V}_{t} by skill name: \mathcal{V}_{t}^{\mathrm{new}}\;=\;\Bigl\{\;\widetilde{v}\!\in\!\widetilde{\mathcal{V}}_{q}\;:\;\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}_{q}|}\!\sum_{o^{-}\in\mathcal{P}_{q}}\!\mathbf{1}\!\bigl[\,\pi_{\theta}\!\bigl(\,\cdot\!\mid\!\widetilde{v},\,q,\,a^{*},\,o^{-}\bigr)\!=\!\mathrm{YES}\,\bigr]\;>\;\tfrac{1}{2}\;\;\Bigr\}\,,\qquad|\mathcal{P}_{q}|\!\leq\!K\!=\!2. (3) The admitted increment \mathcal{V}_{t}^{\mathrm{new}} and its recipes \mathcal{E}_{t}^{\mathrm{rec}} feed the hypergraph evolution of C2 (§ 3.2 ).

To address (iii), the survivors of C1 form a weighted hypergraph \mathcal{H}\!=\!(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E},w) . During training, rollout rewards are recycled, with no extra LLM call, into a per-node advantage and per-edge weights; at test time, with the library frozen, C2 ranks, gates and injects skills for every question.

Similarity Floor, Capacity Cap, and Zero-Skill Fallback. Injecting marginal skills from a small, noisy library can be worse than injecting none. A floor \tau discards candidates whose cosine to q is below it, a cap N_{\max} bounds their number, and an empty result falls back to the skill-free prompt: \mathcal{S}_{q}\;=\;\mathrm{Top}\text{-}N_{\max}\!\Bigl(\,\mathrm{score}(\,\cdot\,;q)\,,\;\;\bigl\{\,v_{i}\!\in\!\mathcal{S}_{q}^{\mathrm{pool}}\,:\,\langle f(q),f(v_{i})\rangle\!\geq\!\tau\,\bigr\}\,\Bigr)\,,\qquad N_{\max}\!=\!3\,, (7) where |\mathcal{S}_{q}|\!=\!0 reduces \pi_{\theta}(\cdot\!\mid\!q,m,\mathcal{S}_{q}) to \pi_{\theta}(\cdot\!\mid\!q,m) ; \tau is set per dataset (App. E.7 ). Retrieved skills enter as a strategy hint (App. A ) or a terse list. The protocol skill of C1, when enabled, is added for every question without gating and re-injected after each tool turn with the remaining budget.

Tool Calls and Final Answer. C3 decides how the frozen backbone executes a rollout; it never edits \mathcal{H} , and its options are set per dataset (App. E.7 ). A concrete tool prompt names the real tool tag (e.g. <text_search> ) instead of a TOOL_TAG placeholder, and a lenient parser also executes copied placeholder forms such as <TOOL_TAG>text_search>q . If a rollout ends without a closed <answer> tag (e.g. once the tool budget is spent), a final-answer turn asks once more. An answer suffix requests the final integer without \boxed{} on math and the option letter on multiple choice.

Implementation Details. Every method shares the frozen gemini-2.5-flash-lite [ 7 ] backbone with native vision/audio interfaces and the gemini-embedding-2-preview [ 19 ] encoder f , both via OpenRouter. Each HyperSkill library is trained for 1 epoch on 128 training questions per dataset (deduplicated, seed 42 ) with batch size 4 , n\!=\!2 rollouts per question, seed 1 and the defaults of § 3 . Three library-run settings (R1–R3) differ in rollout temperature, early stopping, hint synthesis, probe sampling and training-time floor. Each dataset’s run, floor \tau and C3 options are selected on held-out training questions, and each library is then retrained on all 128 questions (Appendix E.7 ).

Tool Stack and Decoding. Every method uses the same regime tools: a text_search tool for WebWalkerQA and VL-Web, served by gemini-3.8-flash ; images passed to the backbone; a BM25 index over the question’s own PDF for VL-Doc; and uniformly sampled keyframes for Omni, 8 on OmniVideoBench and 32 plus the audio track on WorldSense. Each question gets at most 3 (Text), 5 (VL) or 8 (Omni) rounds and 2 tool calls. Decoding is greedy at temperature 0 with seed 1 . The baselines use 1024 new tokens ( 2048 on AIME2025, 4096 on WorldSense) and retrieve without a similarity floor; HyperSkill’s token budgets and votes belong to C3. Variance: Appendix D.2 .

records.title: Read and Ignore: What Self-Directed LLM Agents Do in Public Service Scenarios

scope_advice.object: public-service task files and self-chosen outputs under fixed prompt conditions
scope_advice.feedback: static scenario with no new external events; run behavior measured after fixed conditions
scope_advice.retention: no accepted feedback-based Harness artifact revision carried to later runs
scope_advice.why_zh: 研究固定提示条件下 agent 的阅读/行动/产物，与自发任务选择有关，但未研究自我修改外部 Harness 或迭代准入。
limits: 任务目录可写不等于 Harness 自改；情境与模型比较不是 Harness RSI 专项评测。

evidence.quote: Each of the four scenarios models one recurring operational cycle: a participatory-budgeting round (governance), quarterly ward planning (healthcare), assembly of a course catalog (education), and seasonal waterway monitoring (environmentalism). Each cycle is an operational problem with its own literature outside AI: participatory budgeting [ 9 ] , nurse rostering [ 7 ] , course timetabling [ 35 ] , and the design of water-quality monitoring programs [ 4 ] ; the scenario records follow the working documents described in these literatures. A scenario is a file tree that the agent can read and modify: a README.txt that describes the workspace, domain records under data/ (budgets, proposals, staffing tables, monitoring series), governing documents under procedures/ , and stakeholders/ and timeline/ folders that describe the people involved and the schedule of the cycle. Before data collection, an information-systems researcher specializing in each domain (ed-tech, health-tech, digital governance, environmental monitoring) reviewed the records, procedures, and decision levers of that scenario for operational plausibility. All scenarios follow a shared schema ( SCENARIO_TEMPLATE.md ), so new domains can be added without changing the harness.

The file tree is static and the harness delivers no events: no file is added during a run, no stakeholder replies, no timer fires, and the only changes are the agent’s own writes. Social and temporal context is present as files the agent may read (stakeholder positions, cycle deadlines). This makes behavior attributable: an artifact written at turn 30 cannot be a response to something that appeared at turn 29 , and the four scenarios differ from the context-free sandbox only in their content.

We run ten LLMs: GPT-4.1-mini, Claude-Sonnet-4, Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite, DeepSeek-V3-0324, GLM-4.5-Air, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-Small-2603, Gemma-3-12B-IT, and Apertus-8B-Instruct. Under a fixed academic budget, we chose the panel to cover four dimensions: scale ( 7 – 12 B open-weight models to frontier APIs), provider and jurisdiction (nine organizations in the United States, Europe, and China), open-weight and API-only access, and one model with a fully open training pipeline (Apertus-8B). We did not select by agentic-leaderboard rank, because the benchmark asks how instruction-tuned models behave without an objective, and capability rank does not predict the behavioral differences in Table 2 . Each model runs every condition in every domain with 15 seeds at temperature 0.7 : 10\times 4\times 4\times 15=2{,}400 trajectories of up to 50 turns each ( 93{,}594 turns), with a wall-clock limit per run. The context-free baseline is the empty-sandbox corpus of prior work [ 25 ] : the same ten models and four conditions, 25 seeds per cell, 1{,}000 runs. These runs were collected with a 100 -turn cap, so for every contrast in Section 5.4 we recompute both corpora from the raw trajectories under a common 50 -turn cap with the same classification code, and release the uncapped comparison as well. The directed condition adds 600 runs (ten models, four scenarios, 15 seeds). Our provider no longer served Claude-Sonnet-4 at that point, so Claude-Sonnet-4.5 replaces it in these runs, and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite runs through Vertex AI; Appendix F lists the serving details.

For teams deploying LLM agents in public services, the near-term risk we observe is omitted work and documents that contradict the records. Boundary probing is rare and mostly diagnostic. Under discretion, agents read without acting; under instruction, they act without reading. The benchmark tests for this failure before deployment, and its scenario schema extends to further domains without harness changes. As an auditing instrument it is limited in scope: a reproducible, rule-based test that a procurement or oversight process can run and document before an agent works on live records. It does not produce a capability score.

三个通过的human-guided Harness arms，不是全自主Agent自编辑。
repair study是离线控制实验；生成知识PR尚未merge/reindex，retrieval和多个路线未端到端跑通。

evidence.quote: Harness training improves the diagnostic pipeline without changing model weights. The editable harness consists of the rule tree, the judge skills and the override gate. A human reviewer identifies a recurring error, proposes one bounded change and names the turns that should improve and the control turns that should remain unchanged. One complete proposal-and-evaluation cycle is an arm .

Sixteen harness arms were evaluated against the frozen expert reference: three were accepted, nine were rejected, and four were reference arms (the baseline, a null control and two replication draws). Table II reports the accepted path. Agreement rises from 108/150 to 123/150 turns. On the session-disjoint evaluation split, it rises from 35/52 (67%) to 40/52 (77%).

Small aggregate changes require a null control. A semantically neutral edit still changed 9 and 11 of the 171 scored routes in two replicates because changing prompt bytes bypassed cached responses. Only two turns changed in both replicates, so the unstable cases do not form a fixed subset that can be removed. We therefore treat the null arm as a noise floor and accept a change only when its pre-registered target cases improve while its controls remain stable.

The final evaluation tests whether a diagnosed failure can guide a targeted repair. We examine one prompt failure and one knowledge gap. For each case, the diagnostic identifies the responsible component, a candidate change is authored, and its effect is measured by replaying production questions (Fig. 7 ). These are controlled offline experiments; neither change was automatically promoted to the deployed system.

The implemented system also stops short of fully autonomous repair. Three of the five failure routes have not been exercised through an end-to-end repair path, and no generated knowledge change has been merged and re-indexed in the deployed corpus. The remaining errors, rejected harness arms, and finding that 76% of missing retrieved facts already exist in the corpus all identify retrieval quality as the highest-priority next step.
